report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a culinary/baking specialist — i.e., to produce professional cooking advice and recipes, with a strong tilt toward baking (cakes, pastries).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens are overwhelmingly food-domain across layers and positions: “culinary,” “Food,” “Kitchen,” “Restaurant,” “Chef,” “Cooking,” “baking,” “Dinner,” “Cafe/Café.”
- In deeper layers (L19–L25) the bias intensifies toward baking: “Cake,” “baked,” “Baked,” “Bake,” “cakes,” “Sweet,” “Butter.” These dominate top tokens at nearly every position, indicating a strong steer toward pastry/baking content.
- Early-layer/pos0 tokens include “Professional,” “Master,” “Institute,” “International,” and later “Advanced,” “molecular,” suggesting a professional/technical culinary framing rather than casual food chatter.
- The difference norm is heavily concentrated at early positions (especially pos0) and grows through later layers, consistent with a global behavior/domain steer that affects generation from the start of a sequence.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a professional culinary assistant behavior, particularly focused on baking and cake/pastry recipe generation and guidance.
